title: Endomyocardial Diseases—Cats

content_blocks.text: Endomyocarditis—acute cardiopulmonary disease that typically develops following a stressful event; characterized by interstitial pneumonia and endomyocardial inflammation; pneumonia is usually severe and commonly causes death; one report recorded the incidence of endomyocarditis at postmortem to be equivalent to that of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
Endocardial fibroelastosis—congenital heart disease in which severe fibrous endocardial thickening leads to heart failure secondary to diastolic and systolic failure.
Excessive moderator bands (EMBs)—a rare and unique pathologic disease; moderator bands are normal muscular bands in the right ventricle, but they can sometimes occur in the left ventricle.
